source.title: Noisy Interpolation Learning with Shallow Univariate ReLU Networks
source.authors: Nirmit Joshi; Gal Vardi; N. Srebro

record.tranche_reason: Analyzes noisy interpolation in a new, restricted setting: minimum-weight-norm univariate two-layer ReLU regression. It reports generalization results for that setting, but does not test the listed claim versions about standard deep networks trained by stochastic gradient methods on completely random image labels.
record.gate_note: The paper defines its predictor to interpolate every training example. Its results concern population and reconstruction risk under noisy regression, not image classification, completely random labelings, or SGD. Those results are recorded under fits_no_version. No results are reported for V1–V6 as specified.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes generalization of a minimum-norm univariate two-layer ReLU regression interpolator. Exact training fit is imposed by Eq. (2), rather than established through stochastic-gradient training. Its risk bounds do not test any of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors additionally emphasize that random-input risk is infinite in expectation even below L2, whereas fixed-grid behavior is tempered both in probability and in expectation. Their conclusions concern generalization of prescribed interpolators, not the optimization or learning dynamics of random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies a minimum-weight-norm interpolator with unbounded-width, univariate two-layer ReLU regression and an unregularized skip connection. It does not use the original studies’ image-classification experiments or stochastic-gradient training procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss power p and input sampling scheme (i.i.d. uniform points versus a fixed uniform grid) change the reported generalization behavior; expectation versus high-probability behavior also differs.

fits_no_version.finding: With i.i.d. uniform inputs, risk is bounded with high probability on the scale Lp(f*)/(2−p) for 1≤p<2; Gaussian-noise lower bounds match this dependence. For p≥2, risk diverges in probability under Gaussian noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization of minimum-norm univariate ReLU regression interpolators can change from tempered to catastrophic with the loss exponent.

fits_no_version.finding: With equally spaced inputs, risk is bounded by a constant multiple of the noise risk for every fixed p≥1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-grid sampling yields tempered overfitting for the studied minimum-norm interpolator across Lp losses.

fits_no_version.finding: For random inputs and 1≤p<2, expected population risk is infinite despite the high-probability bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tempered overfitting in probability need not imply tempered overfitting in expectation.

record.problems: The analysis is limited to univariate two-layer ReLU regression with a minimum-norm interpolation rule, rather than standard deep image classifiers trained by SGD. Several results are asymptotic and stated as bounds rather than empirical measurements; the fixed-grid and random-input settings have different behavior.

untested.parts: Stochastic-gradient fitting of completely random labels by standard deep networks, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance-level test error.
Training-time comparison between real and random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance across a sweep of label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing them.
Learning real-data patterns before memorizing noise over the course of training.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its own gate note and should be corrected to discusses/T6. The stated ICLR 2023 publication status is not established by the supplied text; its ICLR 2017 reference is the original Zhang et al. study.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random image labels, test error at chance, standard deep networks, SGD, and unchanged original architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time, convergence speed, and dependence on the fraction of corrupted labels.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep from no corrupted labels to all corrupted labels, perfect training fit across that sweep, and steadily rising test error.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their effect on fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Whether real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.
